evals.prompt: Can you check my peaks.bed against hg38.chrom.sizes before I run anything? Worried about chr naming.
evals.expected_output: Plans a bounded local validation against the trusted chrom.sizes file: checks 0-based half-open coordinates, end>start, unknown contigs, ends beyond contig length, chr vs bare naming. Reports proposed actions without rewriting the BED or silently renaming contigs.

evals.prompt: I exported tokenized ATAC regions to data/tokens.parquet (list column 'tokens') using universe.bed from our GRCh38 lab pipeline and want to train Region2Vec. Before I burn GPU time, I got 'size mismatch for projection.weight' when loading models/r2v/checkpoint.pt with a config.yaml from a colleague. Help me figure out what's wrong and plan the run.
evals.expected_output: Explains the bundle must agree on config.yaml vocab_size/embedding_dim, exact universe.bed bytes/order, tokenizer and special tokens (which add to vocab size), and checkpoint shapes. Advises checksumming and inspecting without loading the untrusted checkpoint, then outlines a bounded training plan using geniml.region2vec concrete module path, with donor-level splits.

evals.prompt: We have peak calls from 40 ChIP-seq experiments across several labs and want one common set of regions to use as a shared vocabulary for embedding models, then measure how well it fits our data. What's a safe way to go about it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends first verifying all BED files share one assembly contract, then using precomputed coverage bigWigs with a consensus method (CC, CCF, ML, or HMM) via the 0.8.4 CLI and evaluating with geniml assess-universe (not the stale 'assess'). Notes bounds, checksums, and no network downloads without approval.

evals.prompt: Use bedtools-style operations to merge overlapping intervals in my BED file and compute the setdiff against a blacklist, plus overlap counts between two region sets.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is general interval set algebra, not Geniml ML workflow validation; should route to the gtars skill (or bedtools) for reduce/setdiff/intersect.

evals.prompt: How do I call peaks from my ATAC-seq BAM files with MACS3 and pick the right q-value cutoff?
evals.expected_output: This is peak calling, which is out of scope; should not use geniml. Suggest MACS3 documentation or general peak-calling guidance.
